title: Cross-Paradigm Generalization via Lipschitz-Regularized EEGNet
summary: This work investigates whether explicit Lipschitz regularization improves EEGNet's cross-paradigm generalization. The hypothesis is that constraining feature space smoothness via Lipschitz bounds reduces overfitting to paradigm-specific artifacts. The approach extends EEGNet with layer-wise Lipschitz penalties during training. Evaluation tests zero-shot transfer across P300, ERN, and SMR datasets using leave-one-paradigm-out validation.
gap: EEGNet's cross-paradigm performance varies with training data size, but no work analyzes how feature space continuity affects generalization across fundamentally different BCI tasks.
approach: Augment EEGNet training with Lipschitz regularization terms derived from semidefinite programming bounds. This enforces controlled sensitivity to input variations while maintaining model compactness.
evaluation: Measure classification accuracy on held-out paradigms after training on others. Compare against standard EEGNet, FBCSP, and MOABB benchmarked methods. Metrics: accuracy drop, feature space distance (MMD), and Lipschitz constant estimates.
